acceptance: The member-level differences between the two v0.5.0 productions are listed (which files, which fields), with the cause: parent-dependent content, timestamps, ordering, or exporter change

Decision recorded: which production docs:pin takes (for example the earliest certified production of the tag commit, or the one whose producing run is the tag's own Trunk-certified build), with the reason
docs:pin implements the rule, records the chosen site-inputs run id in release-pin/pin.json, and `docs:pin -- --check` online confirms that run still holds the pinned manifest or reports it expired
A test shows two productions of one commit in the artifact list and asserts the rule picks the same one regardless of listing order
If the members differ because core's exporters are not deterministic, a core-tracker prompt is written for the owner and linked here; no site code works around it
context: Found 2026-11-14 while reproducing the v0.5.0 pin. Decision gate: the selection rule, after the diff is understood. Guardrails: do not change bundle-fetch selection for deploys (Explorer and deploy gates); do not re-pin v0.5.0; never edit release-pin/ by hand. If first-default-docs-pin-run lands first, check which v0.5.1 production it pinned and record it here.
description:
Problem: core can now build a bundle for a given commit (site-inputs.yml dispatch with core_sha), so one release commit can have several certified bundles. v0.5.0 (commit dfe585e) has two: site-inputs run 42114319044 (2026-11-05, the one pinned) and run 43498628032 (2026-11-13). Pinning from the second changed release-pin/manifest.json: parent_source, produced_at and three member digests differ. `npm run docs:pin -- <tag>` fetches through bundle-fetch with SITE_INPUTS_CORE_SHA, which takes the first unexpired develop artifact of that name, so which production is pinned depends on listing order, and re-running the pin can change the published docs inputs without any core change.

Outcome: the pin is reproducible, and it is known whether two productions of the same commit can differ in docs-data, doc-contracts.json or repo-files.json, which would mean the exporters are not deterministic or depend on the parent.
